> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR

> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/tsup.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 34 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **54** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a43405d596d4d670dc761e90c9fc20822dc806a9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `830416a5d30fdbb4febf6ffc9234211919ed6865` — the merge of head `9f60a2ba3cc5156c9b0722fd95a761adcbe7f187` into base `a43405d596d4d670dc761e90c9fc20822dc806a9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 830416a5d30fdbb4febf6ffc9234211919ed6865 && git checkout 830416a5d30fdbb4febf6ffc9234211919ed6865
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a43405d596d4d670dc761e90c9fc20822dc806a9 9f60a2ba3cc5156c9b0722fd95a761adcbe7f187 && git checkout -B drift-repro a43405d596d4d670dc761e90c9fc20822dc806a9 && git merge --no-ff 9f60a2ba3cc5156c9b0722fd95a761adcbe7f187

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a43405d596d4d670dc761e90c9fc20822dc806a9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a43405d596d4d670dc761e90c9fc20822dc806a9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:services` seat 1 · 2026-10-20T07:17Z

`os-justin` · `session_011TdZ8GjixNZFLz1xJD9zzK` (seat post #6021). Reviewed against GitHub and `origin/main` `a43405d596`, not against the report (os-dev-report on #24739).

**Disclosure read first** (the maintainer's ruling recorded on #9387). The PR body, the changeset and the report give operator guidance and the rule. None carries a bypass path.

Head under review:

```text
9f60a2ba3cc5156c9b0722fd95a761adcbe7f187
```

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #24739`, line-start `Clause-②: no` in the body and the changeset. The only other issue the body names is #9387, with no keyword beside it. 16 files, +689/−70, none on a governed surface (`governedPathsIn` answers `[]`). The trial merge onto `origin/main` is clean.
2. **The rule, read in the code.**
   - `resolveClientAddress` (`@objectstack/plugin-auth/client-address`, dependency-free) reads `X-Forwarded-For`'s first entry, then `X-Real-IP`, only under `trustProxy`; otherwise the transport peer. It is the runtime's rule, moved unchanged. The runtime imports it back with its limiter keys unchanged. The import cannot go the other way because runtime already depends on plugin-auth.
   - That reading is the spec's contract: `server.trustProxy` is "declared `true` ONLY when a reverse proxy you control overwrites those headers on every inbound request" (`stack-server.zod.ts:213`).
   - **D5 gate.** `isClientIpAllowed` now answers `false` for an undetermined address when ranges are set. The middleware answers `403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED`, the out-of-range envelope, and logs one operator line per kind.
   - **D7 audit.** `last_login_ip` reads the address `handleRequest` established, carried in request state, instead of re-reading headers.
   - With no ranges configured, nothing changes.
   - IPv4-mapped peers match their IPv4 range.
3. **Pins and ablations.** `client-ip-allow-list-trust-rule.test.ts` mounts the real raw app and covers:
   - trusted proxy;
   - untrusted proxy;
   - undetermined address, refused with `code` + `status` and one operator line;
   - no ranges configured;
   - an IPv4-mapped peer;
   - D7 with a peer, with a trusted forwarded address, and with none.

   Ablations A1–A4 each turn red as predicted. A1 (the old behaviour) turns 8 red and keeps the trusted-proxy, no-ranges and D7-trusted rows green, which is the preservation half. Every restore was proven by blob equality.
4. **Prose read sentence by sentence against the diff.**
   - **The changeset**, `patch` for plugin-auth, runtime, cli and service-settings:
     - the rule sentence;
     - every operator bullet: declare `trustProxy` before upgrading behind a proxy; the undetermined refusal and its log; `CF-Connecting-IP` no longer read; IPv4-mapped matching; nothing changes without ranges;
     - the `last_login_ip` sentence;
     - each per-package bullet.
   - **`content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`:** the D5 row.
   - **The `allowed_ip_ranges` help text** in `auth.manifest.ts` and its three translations.
   - **The `allowedIpRanges` TSDoc:** the fail-open sentence is gone.
5. **Gates.** At ACCEPT, every check-run on this head is `success` or an expected skip, including TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core 1–6/6, Build Core and Governed Surface Queue Guard. Locally, 116 of 116 derived families exited 0.
6. **The dev's open questions, answered by the seat.**
   - **Where the rule lives:** A, the plugin-auth subpath. Two consumers are measured, and A adds no new package edge. Revisit only if a third consumer appears.
   - **How the raw-app mounts learn the peer:** A, mirroring the transport's six-line reader. A drift fails closed: refusal plus the operator line.
   - **How `trustProxy` reaches the gate:** A, an explicit `AuthManagerOptions.trustProxy` passed by `objectstack serve`. This is the seam the dispatcher already uses.
   - **ADR-0069 D5's mechanism cell and the spec's `server.trustProxy` describe, which names one consumer:** both now under-describe the code. That follow-up is prose only (`docs/adr` and `packages/spec`, the spec seat's surface), filed once this lands.
   - **Clause-② and semver:** A, `no` and `patch`. Publication in this repo's contract sense is `packages/spec`, which this PR does not edit. The new plugin-auth subpath and options are implementation API. The narrowing (an undetermined address refused) is a runtime security behaviour the maintainer directed (filing gate ③). Triage graded it patch-eligible, and the changeset states the operator step plainly.
7. **Accepted deviations.**
   - The claim surface is amended to cover:
     - `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`, one option line;
     - `packages/runtime/src/security/inbound-rate-limit.ts`, pre-declared in the claim.

     Both files are `domain:cli`'s, declared on #22648 (`6285254652`).
   - Also inside the amendment: `service-settings`' help text in four locales and `authentication.mdx`, prose this change made false.
   - The local runtime suite was narrowed to the 11 files that exercise the rule; CI runs the rest.
   - One merge of `main`.
   - Commit trailers are model-free, per AGENTS.md.
8. **Out-of-scope dispositions.**
   - The vendored auth library's own client-address reader does not follow `server.trustProxy`: filed #24799 (abstract only, under the #9387 ruling).
   - D5 coverage on HTTP doors into `handleRequest` other than plugin-auth's own route: `Acceptance notes`.
   - `docs/HARDENING.md`'s hand-written limiter example: `Acceptance notes`.
9. **Landing clause.** Tier S: not governed, under the human-merge threshold. Next step: ready + auto-merge through the relay once every check on the current head is green or an expected skip. A push resets this reading.
